canal_p09_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_001.text: On the eighteenth morning, the cooper arrived at Han's yard in a cart that looked too small for his own shoulders. He had brought a measuring rope, a purse and no intention of buying the canal. Bao inspected the unused private hoist before anybody discussed its price. The old bearings turned cleanly after ordinary lubrication, and its current marked load remained readable. Han watched every check as if the timber could decide which version of his future he would be allowed to keep.

canal_p09_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_002.text: The hoist had belonged to the canceled store extension. Unlike the main crane, it had never swung over the public path or loaded the common wall. Its bolts and fittings stayed inside Han's movable private inventory. Bao gave the cooper the current inspection report and required a ground setup check before any later use in the new yard. A tool fit for sale did not carry a certificate for every future installation. The cooper understood because his own yard wall already had enough things leaning against it.

canal_p09_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_003.text: The inspected hoist and four sound extension planks drew a sixteen-copper offer, twelve for the gear and four for the timber. The cooper could take delivery on the fortieth day after his own foundations were ready. He would pay then against receiving checks, with no cash advanced today. Han accepted the conditional purchase rather than calling the promised amount collected. The spare goods would stay in his high dry store until loading. His return plan now had a specific buyer and date, but its actual purse still held thirty-two.

canal_p09_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_004.text: The broker came before the purchase note's ink dried. He offered immediate cash for the remaining fifty-six toll claim under his final quoted discount, without adding a right over the households. Han read it one last time and declined. He would try to keep the slow valid share while settling the private deposit through the received thirty-two and later sixteen. The broker asked whether he understood that an uncompleted sale was still a risk. Han said yes. He was choosing the risk of waiting without pretending it had vanished.

canal_p09_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_005.text: Tian expected the broker to threaten the bank after being refused. He folded his papers and said another lender upriver might buy the claim later if Han changed his mind. A lawful offer could end without becoming a punishment. Yue watched him leave and realized she had cast his polished sleeves as an omen from the first market. He had pressed hard for a bargain. He had also removed the unauthorized fee when its flaw was shown. Han remained responsible for the private decision he chose after reading it.

canal_p09_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_006.text: The cooper marked the reserved goods with removable tags, not his ownership seal. Title and final acceptance would pass at the actual receiving sale. Han could continue storing them but would notify him before any use that changed their condition. The private buyer's agent copied the proposed delivery date into his deposit schedule and preserved the current contract deadline. Sixteen promised for day forty still left room before term closure. Yue saw how a useful interval could become a plan, provided every person knew what had not happened yet.

canal_p09_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_007.text: Bao returned to the public spill pocket after finishing Han's separately paid private inspection. The original repair order covered its ordinary preparation with the purchased second timber length, spare fittings, the small side-release and sealing material. The upper pocket was small enough for the first controlled trial to stop above the current gardens. A temporary lower stop would keep its test water inside the checked reach. The later whole diversion route needed the downstream visit on the twenty-fourth day. Yue touched the dry side of the warped old board and found it crumbled under her nail.

canal_p09_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_008.text: The new stop board needed a straight seated edge and ordinary bracing against the test head. Bao measured the slots before setting it on the dry bench. One guide post leaned slightly after years of silt pressure. He would not ask the board to correct that lean by bending under water. A fitted packing piece could restore the current small-test alignment without certifying the post for a flood. The working drawing gained a measured limit that Yue would have missed if she trusted the old channel's appearance of being patiently unchanged.

canal_p09_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_009.text: Luo showed the current applicants the ground observation positions above the pocket. The water marks would be read from stable paving, with no one standing in the test channel. Each observer needed a clear view and an ordinary walking retreat to the upper landing. The bank had used its hired tow days at the gate, so Bao and Yue would handle the light dry preparation within their remaining accepted hours. Powered trial work would wait for Jiang's booked supervised appointment. Nothing in the canceled service lot could supply extra hands by implication.

canal_p09_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_010.text: A former founding worker offered to help clear roots because he knew the old hollow. Luo welcomed his site knowledge and asked whether he wanted a current paid task, a short voluntary visit or only to show the old path. He chose the visit and walked from the stable upper bank. His memory located an inspection cover beneath dried reeds. Bao checked its actual position against the plan before opening it. The man's useful past made him worth hearing, not a person whose whole day belonged to their repair.

canal_p09_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_011.text: Inside the cover, the upper pocket's outlet slot held compacted dry roots and a broken pottery shard. The roots had grown through an unsealed side opening. Bao removed only the reachable obstruction with ordinary tools and fitted the planned small seal. Yue carried the light root waste to its container. The pottery belonged to nobody they could name; its glazed edge explained how it could catch fibers without explaining who dropped it. Tian said somebody would still call it a clue. Bao said it was a clue to where the water could stick.

canal_p09_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_012.text: The old worker looked at the reopened slot and remembered clearing it during the fourth annual season. He had not returned because the later lists called his son instead. His son worked at a kiln elsewhere and ignored the request. Pei would preserve that offered account if he wanted, but today's root clearance did not require another search through family blame. Luo asked whether he wished his path note copied for the next keeper. He did, then went home before the bank could turn his useful morning into a whole free shift.

canal_p09_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_013.text: By noon, the sun heated the dry pocket enough that its exposed clay cracked at the edges. Yue wanted to wet it before the trial to see how much seepage changed. Bao agreed a small ordinary measured bucket test could be useful once the new stop was seated, but not today while its fitting remained incomplete. Her next interesting observation depended on someone finishing wood and bracing first. She used the waiting time to copy the retreat path rather than performing a little experiment whose water would find the unprotected gap.

canal_p09_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_014.text: Tian arrived with the applicants' final replies. The morning-only observer wanted a clear ending time; the young rope candidate had passed his examination but accepted no extra bank job; the woman visiting her recovering sister remained unavailable. Luo fit the current observer requirements to actual named staff and the remaining hours. The mother of one applicant wanted a household acknowledgment for the offered shift. Tian explained that the actual worker would receive its wage record. The family could keep that copy if the worker chose, without reopening a household obligation.

canal_p09_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_015.text: The clerk converted the ordinary labor line into accepted hours for the remaining schedule. The twenty-eight worker-days meant their posted day equivalents, spread across the eight-week term. Jiang's short bench visits and two gate appointments consumed two of her three equivalents; the supervised upper trial used the remaining one. Bao and Yue had later preparation hours reserved, with Tian's accepted preparation day already complete. This made the calendar less tidy but the wages more accurate. An afternoon's presence would not secretly purchase someone's next morning for free.

canal_p09_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_016.text: One trustee wanted the old worker's volunteered path visit counted toward the repair workforce, reducing the wage expense. Luo said the approved labor line paid actual hired hours; an offered short visit did not manufacture an employee or authorize withholding another person's wage. The trustee withdrew the suggestion after seeing the worker's limited offered task. Yue appreciated the keeper's firmness because the mistake sounded frugal rather than cruel. The canceled pledge could return through an attractive saving if nobody noticed how differently the hands had been offered.

canal_p09_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_017.text: A cart brought the ordinary bracing clamps already listed in the material purchase. Their maker had packed three useful pieces and one demonstration sample. Bao checked the supplied count before storing the sample separately for return. Yue had nearly entered all four as equipment available for the trial. The sample's thin jaw would not carry the rated bracing load. Tian tied a bright wrapper around it and wrote its return reference. One handsome extra part could make a dangerous inventory if beauty counted as specification.

canal_p09_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_018.text: Han asked whether the bank wanted his unused hoist before the cooper took it. Bao's prepared pocket work did not need its lifting capacity, and the ordinary frame had its own rated actuator for the small side-release. Borrowing an extra machine would add inspection and control tasks without improving the current plan. Han looked disappointed. He wanted to make his private settlement useful to the common bank. Luo thanked him for offering and declined. The gesture could count as goodwill without being accepted into a job where it had no purpose.

canal_p09_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_019.text: The coopering customer came back with a revised delivery route because his original cart could not carry the hoist safely on its small axle. He would book a larger rated cart at his own receiving cost. The sixteen price remained for the inspected goods, paid at actual delivery. Han wrote the changed route beside the storage tags. Yue saw both men protect the sale by admitting an ordinary transport limit instead of placing too much on the cart that brought the buyer's first hopeful purse.

canal_p09_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_020.text: Near the pocket, a young observer found a shallow hollow under the stable path's outer edge. Bao checked it from the sound inner paving and placed a barrier around the uncertain strip. The retreat route shifted inward before any water test. A small old root had held loose soil in place until today's clearing exposed the gap. Nobody had to fall for the observation to matter. Yue redrew the walking line and recorded the new limit beside the old path memory. Current ground would get the final word.

canal_p09_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_021.text: Luo notified the landing keeper of the narrowed walking line so market visitors would not discover it by pressing against the work cord. The public detour remained usable on its inner side at the posted ordinary limit. The bank would price the outer paving repair separately if it proved larger than the current material and staff allowance. Bao could make the small surface secure for the trial observers inside the checked route. He did not promise to restore the whole old edge because the commission already owned a convenient calendar.

canal_p09_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_022.text: At supper, the former founding worker returned with a note about the old inspection cover. He had written its distance from the keeper's corner and drawn the reed bed as it looked twenty-one years ago. Yue thanked him and added the present cover position on a separate current plan. The old reed bed had moved. His note was a useful record of memory offered today, not another hidden original charter map. He wanted both drawings kept. Pei gave them dated covers, leaving the past visible without letting it govern today's water.

canal_p09_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_023.text: On the nineteenth morning, the new stop board seated in the measured guide with its current packing and braces. Bao checked the ordinary fastenings against the planned test head. The small bucket comparison could proceed after Luo closed the feeder and confirmed the isolated pocket dry. Yue measured the offered water in a checked container and poured from the safe upper edge. It spread into the shallow clay unevenly, vanishing first around a dry crack rather than racing obediently toward the outlet mark.

canal_p09_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_024.text: The initial measured bucket test showed soak loss greater than Yue expected. Bao repeated only the small ordinary amount specified for comparison, leaving no live feeder open. The wetted crack took less on its second pour, but their actual sample remained too small to establish flood behavior. Yue copied both amounts and the wet area rather than averaging them into a single confident leakage figure. The powered trial's purpose would be to observe its bounded pocket at the checked head. It would not certify the entire diversion by making one little crack disappear.

canal_p09_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_025.text: Tian watched the sample vanish and said the canal was drinking before offering anybody else a turn. Yue smiled, then realized the phrase would travel faster than her careful measurements. She explained the small dry-clay comparison to the nearby observer who had heard it. Tian helped give the practical version without resenting the correction. They kept the joke for supper and the actual test limits for the work board. It felt good to have a friendship in which accuracy did not always arrive as a public embarrassment.

canal_p09_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_026.text: Jiang's reply confirmed her twentieth-day dry apparatus inspection before the booked live trial. That brief preparatory visit belonged inside her remaining accepted trial equivalent, with its hours preserved for the actual powered work on the twenty-second day. She wanted the supply case opened only with the appropriate current control and frame inspections. Yue had recovered since the gate command, but recovery did not make a prepared apparatus appear checked. She copied the visit time beside the actual retreat route and went to sharpen the ordinary measuring peg.

canal_p09_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_027.text: The day offered three useful jobs before the dry inspection. Bao needed the new stop's witness marks checked without changing its brace positions. Luo needed the updated inner walking route delivered to the landing crews. Tian wanted help finishing the applicant handover copies, including the actual ending times and unaccepted offers. The ordinary crew would report each completed task to the clerk. Yue could work close to the timber, close to the moving feet or close to the people whose chosen hours kept the plan honest.

canal_p09_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_028.text: Yue had watched the old worker offer memory without becoming labor and Han offer a hoist without getting it into the plan. Both offers mattered because they could be declined. Today's chosen task had the same modest freedom. Bao waited with the fastening marks, Luo with the current route notice and Tian with the work replies. The pocket would not receive live feeder water before its checks. Meanwhile the bank could become ready by doing small things carefully enough that people trusted its next larger question.

canal_p09_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_029.text: The new stop waited above a shallow patch of wet clay. Yue could check its ordinary witness marks with Bao, walk the altered retreat notice with Luo or complete actual worker handovers with Tian. Each task had named receivers and a finite ending. Han's thirty-two remained in his private return envelope, the surplus sale stayed conditional for day forty, and the canal's old labor provision stayed complete. The next water would have to travel a prepared path rather than a story everybody wished true.

choices.text: Check the stop's witness marks with Bao.
Walk the altered retreat notices with Luo.
Finish actual worker handovers with Tian.

canal_p09_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_030.text: Bao asked Yue to compare the brace's witness marks with the dry drawing while he checked the opposite fastenings. The first mark looked displaced until she realized the ink line lay on a removable washer, not the fixed post. Turning the washer could mimic movement without changing the brace. Bao replaced that unreliable witness with a line crossing the actual fixed faces. Yue noted the alteration and felt a little angry at the old mark for looking so authoritative in such a convenient place.

canal_p09_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_031.text: The second brace had a true small shift at its lower seating. Bao lowered the unloaded fitting to its dry support before loosening anything. An old pebble beneath the foot had fractured during seating and left a narrow gap. He removed the fragments, restored the planned ordinary packing and retightened the assembly at its specified position. Yue watched the new mark close across the fixed faces. The fault had appeared before water pressed against it, which was the point of checking while the world still made correction easy.

canal_p09_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_032.text: Tian came with tea and wanted to know whether the missed pebble meant the first inspector had been careless. Bao said the pebble looked sound before load, but the current dry seating test revealed it. The record should state the actual sequence. Yue had once disliked answers that refused a culprit. Today she could see the split stone beside the restored brace and accept a fault that belonged to material behavior plus a useful later check. Tian left the tea outside the work surface and went back to her copies.

canal_p09_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_033.text: A carpenter's apprentice at the landing asked to watch the unloaded fitting check. Bao agreed from the marked safe position and made him repeat the clear route before approaching. The boy wanted to climb the stop board to inspect its top edge. Bao gave him the ordinary mirror gauge from the ground instead. Yue helped him set its viewing angle. He found the top fastener through its reflection and grinned. Learning could still feel like a discovery when it used something small instead of putting a person where the next load would be.

canal_p09_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_034.text: The sealing cord had compressed unevenly along one dry corner. Yue read the earlier measured gap and thought the new fitted face might be wrong. Bao showed where a twist in the cord created the raised section. He replaced only that short fitted run from the purchased spare sealing material, then repeated the dry contact check. The gap matched again. Yue copied the actual replacement length. A fitting's failure could be corrected without replacing a whole board merely because a whole board made a more satisfying purchase.

canal_p09_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_035.text: Bao asked Yue to explain the temporary stop's accepted use as if she were giving the keeper handover. She began saying it held water back, then caught the scale missing from her answer. It held the specified upper test pocket at the checked small head, with the downstream stop and walking route prepared. It had not been accepted for a flood. Bao nodded and asked where her ordinary retreat went. She pointed to the inner paving, where the new hollow no longer sat disguised beneath the original path.

canal_p09_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_036.text: On the upper bank, a child had tied a red thread around one survey peg to make it prettier. The thread hid its current measured face. Yue asked him to move it onto a safe unused offcut outside the test marks. He agreed after she gave him the actual reason instead of claiming all official wood was sacred. Bao rechecked the peg against its reference because a hidden mark invited a wrong reading. The child kept the thread and the bank kept the measurement, which seemed a reasonable end to the problem.

canal_p09_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_037.text: The afternoon wind carried dust over the fitted cord. Bao covered the prepared stop while the nearby cart lane was swept at its ordinary working time. Yue wanted to postpone sweeping, then saw flour spilled where a walker could slip. They arranged the cover and kept both jobs rather than making one official test outweigh every ordinary hazard on the path. A landing worker waited until the cover was tied before lifting his broom. He had not been hired to serve the trial, but the brief coordination made his own work safer too.

canal_p09_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_038.text: Jiang's arrival note reached them through Luo. She wanted the corrected witness-mark drawing and actual brace shift in the dry inspection report. Yue copied the change plainly, leaving the first unreliable washer mark visible in the comparison section. Bao said a later operator should not have to discover their correction by wondering why the old drawing looked different. He checked the completed stop one last time and left it covered at its current dry support. Water would wait for the actual apparatus inspection.

canal_p09_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_039.text: Yue delivered the fixed witness marks, split pebble fragments and short seal replacement entry to the clerk. None altered the current test head or enlarged the pocket's permitted route. They made the prepared ordinary fitting more dependable. Bao would show Jiang the actual seated brace tomorrow. Yue washed dust from her hands and found she could remember the sound of the pebble breaking more vividly than any clause from the hearing. The work had begun teaching her through things that stayed changed after she stopped looking.

canal_p09_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_040.text: Luo gave Yue the updated walking notice and took the lower landing copy herself. The current safe route used the inner paving, leaving the newly exposed outer hollow fenced. Yue wanted a larger warning banner, but the keeper asked her to place the notice where arriving walkers actually slowed. They chose the turn beside the toll step. Its ordinary sight line mattered more than its size. Yue checked it from the path and saw how easily she had been planning for readers already standing in the office.

canal_p09_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_041.text: A man carrying two baskets tried to use the fenced outer edge because it looked like the shorter line. Yue met him before the barrier and showed the ordinary inner route. He said the new board was an inconvenience invented by people without loads. She took one empty basket at his request while he turned the loaded one through the wider inner corner. The physical help proved the route more clearly than an explanation. He still grumbled, and the path remained safer with him grumbling on it.

canal_p09_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_042.text: At the upper landing, the keeper asked whether the narrow line could take a whole waiting boat crew. Luo's posted ordinary crowd limit still applied, with the lower waiting apron available for overflow. Yue showed the marked stopping place and called the landing receiver to confirm it. The receiver had assumed the closure left no workable waiting space at all. They corrected that misunderstanding together before the evening arrivals. A warning that hid the available safe choice would turn a small closure into a rumor much larger than the hollow.

canal_p09_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_043.text: The egg seller from the gate detour came back with an empty basket and recognized Yue. She asked whether the cart route still ran now the lock reopened. It did, under its own posted service times. Yue introduced her to the current receiver rather than answering every future schedule from memory. The woman wanted the same clean cart bed before tomorrow's eggs. She inspected it herself and booked the offered time. Yue liked seeing a person keep the judgment the bank once helped her begin.

canal_p09_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_044.text: A fisher heard that the upper spill pocket would receive trial water and feared it would wash down into his evening nets. Yue showed the actual lower stop and bounded trial reach on the notice. The present trial would not cross the downstream closure. The later route required the gardens' visit and current survey. He asked who would tell him if the plan changed. Luo's landing receiver accepted that contact under the fisher's offered name. His concern entered a current route instead of being dismissed as someone else's faraway problem.

canal_p09_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_045.text: Two boys imitated the observer's retreat call while running toward the fenced edge. Yue stopped them from the inner path and asked them to move their game onto the open apron. Their grandmother came to collect them and said official words made every game exciting. Yue gave them an ordinary empty crate lid for a pretend gate only after its owner agreed. The grandmother watched them set it well away from the working route. A public warning could need a children's explanation without becoming a public scolding of their whole family.

canal_p09_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_046.text: At the lower landing, a tired porter read the new notice and said he would need a rest stop before the inner turn. Luo pointed to the level apron where loads could be set down outside the gate line. Yue helped the porter check the actual distance with his current burden. He chose that route and asked for a small rest marker rather than a special escort. The receiver placed one at the agreed side. The bank's walking line gained a practical detail no map of the old charter would have supplied.

canal_p09_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_047.text: The fenced hollow attracted a knot of curious market visitors. One said she could see a hidden tunnel beneath the soil. Bao's actual inspection had shown loose earth at the outer edge, not an explored passage. Yue read the current description and offered the viewing point from stable paving without allowing a closer crowd. The woman lost interest when no tunnel appeared in the words. Yue hoped she would tell the same smaller story later. The notice could be accurate even when its audience preferred mystery.

canal_p09_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_048.text: Luo met Yue at the counter with the lower landing report. Both crews knew the altered route, waiting limits and actual receiver for later changes. The fisher's contact and porter's rest marker joined the current handover. Yue had carried more than a sheet. She had watched bodies trying to use a plan on ordinary feet. The test pocket still waited dry beneath its cover. Its future water would move through a place whose ground choices had become clearer before anything needed to escape.

canal_p09_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_049.text: Yue gave the clerk the path handover and the two offered contact changes. Luo asked whether she had walked the route with an actual load after the basket turn. Yue had, briefly, and recorded the experience without presenting it as a complete load test for every porter. The inner paving remained accepted at its posted ordinary use. The added rest point made it more usable. Tomorrow's apparatus operator would find fewer people guessing where they were supposed to stand when an ordinary test began.

canal_p09_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_050.text: Tian opened the handover copies on her stitching table after moving the paid sail order clear. She wanted each worker to receive the actual task and ending time, but her own workroom now held too many bank papers. Yue began sorting them by reference. Tian said she had asked for help carrying the finished copies, not turning her evening into another office. Yue stopped with one sheet halfway across the table. She had heard a task request and silently enlarged it because the larger arrangement looked more efficient.

canal_p09_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_051.text: The awkward silence lasted until Yue put the paper back. She asked where Tian wanted the copied sheets kept before delivery. Tian chose the clean crate near the door and returned the paid cloth to its own frame. Yue moved only the offered stack. A few hours of useful public work had made her forget that this room supported someone else's private rent. The hearing had been about exactly that sort of convenience. Knowing the principle did not keep her from stepping over a smaller version when she was tired.

canal_p09_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_052.text: Tian said she had enjoyed helping the gate and still wanted an evening without the canal occupying her whole table. Yue agreed, then nearly explained how much other people needed the copies. She bit back the explanation because need was not an answer to the time Tian had offered. They checked the finished handovers at the doorway, where the light was worse but the workroom remained free. The bank would survive a less elegant sorting surface. Tian's sale order needed the clean table tonight.

canal_p09_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_053.text: The first worker wanted to change a morning task to late afternoon. Tian showed the actual observation interval and explained why its light and staffing could not simply move. The worker declined that current shift, then offered a later preparation hour instead. Bao would consider it within the remaining task plan. Yue did not mark the replacement accepted while waiting for his answer. The woman thanked Tian for a clear refusal, saying an uncertain yes had once cost her a paid boat job elsewhere.

canal_p09_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_054.text: A man's handover copy had the right task but his brother's landing address. Tian had copied the household reference from the old list by habit. She corrected it after asking his actual current receiver. Yue felt relieved that someone else made a visible mistake, then ashamed of the relief. Tian laughed when Yue admitted both feelings. They wrote the offered address properly and kept the correction on the clerk's comparison copy. Friendship could hold an ordinary error without using it as evidence that one person should stop learning.

canal_p09_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_055.text: The morning-only observer asked for the trial's stopping rule in plain speech. Yue explained that the test would end at the scheduled mark or earlier if the apparatus, stop board or observed flow left its checked conditions. The worker wanted to know whether he could call a stop from his position without waiting for Yue. Bao's plan allowed any observer to give the agreed warning. Tian made that line visible on his copy. The small authority mattered more to him than being called a member of a brave crew.

canal_p09_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_056.text: The newer preparation worker asked whether his completed gate day qualified him to take a powered-control position now. Yue said Jiang would require the actual apparatus training, which his ordinary preparation had not supplied. He accepted a current handover observation instead and asked where he could pursue the training later. Tian gave him the workshop's public contact from Jiang's note, leaving the admission decision there. The bank could help him find a route without making the next stage appear because the trial needed more convenient qualified hands.

canal_p09_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_057.text: One handover recipient asked Tian to speak for him at every later maintenance meeting because he disliked rooms full of louder people. She offered to read his particular written reply if he wanted, but could not hold a permanent authority he never had time to review. He chose a specific current note about ending times and kept future decisions open. Yue carried that offered note to the clerk. The old household list had made enduring representation look natural. Their current invitation could remain smaller and therefore more useful.

canal_p09_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_058.text: Bao answered the changed preparation-hour request before dusk. It fit beside the remaining dry fitting check and used actual unspent accepted hours, replacing an earlier unfilled task interval. Tian delivered the approved task copy and removed the declined morning slot from the worker's sheet. No invisible person remained in the emptied place. Yue asked whether they could return the rest of the papers to the counter now. Tian said yes with such obvious relief that Yue laughed. The paid sail order would finally have the table to itself.

canal_p09_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_059.text: At the counter, Yue gave the clerk the corrected address, changed accepted hour and specific worker reply. Tian went back to her stitching room without another canal stack. Their afternoon had left a bruise in the conversation and a better understanding of how easily useful help could become occupation. Yue promised to ask what help was actually wanted next time, then stopped before making the promise grander. She would practice it at the next ordinary table. Tonight Tian had her own work, and Yue would finish elsewhere.

canal_p09_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_060.text: The completed afternoon reports met at the counter before the twentieth morning's inspection. The stop's witness marks were dependable, the altered walking route had current receivers, and actual workers held their task copies. One changed preparation hour fit the remaining schedule. Yue heard the jobs she had not followed from the people who completed them. The old worker's path memory stayed dated in Pei's store, and the live feeder remained closed to the upper pocket. The bank was ready for Jiang to ask a different set of practical questions.

canal_p09_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_061.text: Jiang arrived on the twentieth morning carrying a little tin of sour plums because she knew the keeper's tea became stronger the longer a meeting lasted. Luo accepted the plums and asked if that was a criticism. Jiang said it was an adaptation. Yue laughed before remembering that apparatus inspections also began with adaptations more sensible than stubbornness. The case stayed closed until the ordinary fitted stop and ground route were shown. The bright tin made the morning feel less like an examination she needed to pass personally.

canal_p09_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_062.text: Bao showed the split packing pebble, corrected fixed witness marks and actual lower stop. Jiang asked him to describe the accepted head without pointing to the old charter. He gave the current measured limit and the bounded pocket volume. The gardens remained protected beyond the closure. She then walked the observer path with Luo, noting the newly fenced hollow and safe inner apron. Yue followed with the report sheet, hearing the dry inspection build on actual work instead of starting every question again from a suspicious blank.

canal_p09_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_063.text: At the apparatus contact box, one ordinary terminal had loosened during transport. Jiang isolated the supply, checked the lead and refastened it under its specified fitting. Yue had wanted the frame opened immediately because its gauge record looked reassuring. The loose terminal explained why charge count and dependable delivery were different checks. Jiang repeated the unloaded selector travel after repair, using the hand control. No live command from Yue was needed to reveal or fix the fault. The inspection cost attention rather than another performance.

canal_p09_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_064.text: The frame's ordinary guard had a latch that Bao's old tool cloth could catch during movement. Tian took the cloth away from the working corner and provided a plain clean cover outside the guard. Jiang checked the latch's full travel with the contact box closed. Yue wrote the actual clearance rather than simply ticking 'covered.' A protective cover could make a new snag if placed badly. The job seemed crowded with small things capable of undoing one another, and none cared how noble the canceled service notice had been.

canal_p09_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_065.text: Jiang accepted the dry control path after its repeated unloaded checks and read the supply gauge against the current reference. The six stones still held two hundred sixteen units. Today's mechanical inspection had used hand movement and no powered draw. Live trial would be limited to the scheduled upper stop response, not a general test of everything water could do. Yue asked which part she could control. Jiang showed one prepared side-release into the checked catch, with its ordinary manual equivalent. The rest of the trial would belong to observers and measured flow.

canal_p09_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_066.text: Luo assembled the actual observers for the stopping-call rehearsal. Each gave the agreed word from the position where he or she would stand, then walked the ordinary clear retreat to the upper apron. One worker's call disappeared beneath a passing cargo shout. They waited for the boat to move and repeated the exercise with the nearer relay speaker in place. The live trial would occur only after ordinary cargo traffic was held clear for its booked interval. A good signal needed a real chance to be heard.

canal_p09_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_067.text: Han heard the rehearsal from his store and complained that stopping the market for another test would cost trade. Luo showed the short booked interval and ordinary alternatives, not an unlimited repair closure. Han accepted after checking his own scheduled cargo. The private gear observation week would continue outside that trial period. Yue understood why the bank could not satisfy every business timetable at once. It could describe a genuine limited interruption and let people plan around it. Han grumbled while making that plan, which was still cooperation.

canal_p09_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_068.text: The inner-path rest marker helped a porter waiting nearby keep his loaded basket clear of the observer line. He asked whether he could remain to watch. Luo showed him the public viewing place outside the work area and said it might offer nothing more interesting than a small board moving. He said he had watched worse entertainment at a paid festival. Tian laughed and set the viewing boundary. The trial would have witnesses without making curiosity into another loaded body where an operator needed room.

canal_p09_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_069.text: Pei delivered the offered old path note and kept its separate memory date visible. Jiang read it after the current plan, using it to ask about a buried corner rather than allowing it to determine today's outlet. Bao had already checked that accessible corner and sealed the small side opening. The old worker's memory helped confirm where to look. The actual dry inspection confirmed what was presently there. Yue liked the sequence: the person remained useful, and the ground retained its stubborn right to disagree with him.

canal_p09_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_070.text: Before noon, Jiang gave the clerk the dry apparatus acceptance and listed the remaining pre-trial conditions. The current fitting, observer rehearsal and supply gauge were checked; the feeder head and lower stop would be checked again immediately before live water. A scheduled time did not eliminate those last observations. The trial would proceed on the twenty-second day if its conditions held. Yue recorded the actual appointment and told the morning-only observer when his accepted interval ended, preserving the stopping time he had insisted on seeing.

canal_p09_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_071.text: That afternoon, Han sent the cooper the current storage check and accepted conditional purchase copy. The reserved hoist and four planks remained sound in the high dry store. The delivery cart was booked for day forty, with its actual axle and load allowance stated. Han's thirty-two deposit-return copper remained set aside. The buyer's agent acknowledged the plan and asked for notice if anything changed. Yue could see a private deadline held through ordinary correspondence, separate from the upper pocket's public water.

canal_p09_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_072.text: Tian finished the sail order and received its second payment on time. Her room rent was now covered by actual paid stitching rather than expected money. She brought Yue a small square of leftover clean cloth for wrapping the measuring peg, after the owner agreed she could keep the offcut. Yue asked whether she wanted anything done at the table before taking it. Tian said no, smiling at the question. The question gave her room to finish her own work. Their friendship felt easier when small requests could stay small.

canal_p09_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_073.text: The missing-name comparison continued at the counter with the possible counterfoil's offered number. Pei and the owner found the final mark belonged to a different seasonal reference. It would not restore the scratched-through name. The owner accepted the result and kept the paper as her family's actual receipt. The narrow public request stayed open for its original reference. Yue felt less urgency to force an ending onto it now. The completed collective pledge stayed released while one person's historical name still waited for the right evidence.

canal_p09_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_074.text: Luo received a weather note from the upper landing: a distant ridge had a brief shower, with no current rise at the canal mark. The note was ordinary observation from its actual receiver, not a spirit's forecast. She added the source and time to the keeper log, then checked the feeder herself. Bao's trial limit stayed unchanged. Later higher water would require another response, but today's weather did not grant them either panic or complacency. Yue put the current reading beside the trial's actual preconditions.

canal_p09_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_075.text: After supper, the observers discussed their work without a public audience. One said he always feared being the person who called stop too soon. Another feared being ignored when he called at all. Jiang said the rehearsal gave them a shared procedure, but the actual operator still had to honor it. Yue understood the warning because she wanted the trial to succeed. She would have to notice that desire in time to stop it from arguing against a voice whose whole useful task was to interrupt her.

canal_p09_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_076.text: The seedling on Tian's window had settled into its pot and lost one leaf while keeping another firm. Yue asked if that counted as success. Tian said it counted as a plant with two different results. They ate the last sour plum from Jiang's tin and discussed nothing about the canal for a while. Tian described a customer who wanted a seam invisible from both sides and cheaper than thread. Yue laughed until her shoulders loosened. Rest finally arrived without being disguised as another lesson.

canal_p09_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_077.text: Before bed, Yue checked her ordinary practice baseline on the unpowered tile. Her opened arm pairs had recovered from the gate sequence, and the route she would use at the live trial stayed within its established small command and delivery allowance. She put the tile away instead of repeating the sensation because it felt reassuring. Tomorrow's dry prechecks belonged to her ordinary work. The live response would come the day afterward, if actual water and equipment conditions allowed it. Her body did not owe the schedule a better result than it had earned.

canal_p09_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p09_078.text: At dusk, Bao left the upper stop covered, its current witness marks visible and its dry path clear. Luo posted the short trial interval at both landings and held cargo bookings outside it. Han closed his private store after checking the tagged hoist. Tian returned her paid cloth order and Pei locked the amended receiving pages. Yue looked from the repaired gate toward the small pocket beyond it. The first diversion trial would now ask whether prepared wood, counted supply and actual people could keep a promise the old map had never tested.
